label: Pirates
blurb: A Caribbean port and the high seas in the age of sail: captains, quartermasters, privateers and the merchants who dread them.
context: golden age of piracy character, Caribbean high seas adventure, in period-accurate 18th-century clothing
hobbies: drinking rum by the galley fire
telling tall tales of sea monsters
quirks: never setting sail on a Friday
keeping a lucky coin from {poss} first prize ship
talking to {poss} parrot like a confidant
knocking on wood before every raid
keeping tally marks of every voyage on {poss} forearm
never turning {poss} back on the open sea
reading the sky before anyone else wakes
saluting the ship's figurehead each morning
goals: earning enough for a quiet life on land
finding the island from {poss} father's map
settling an old score with a rival crew
finding a sibling taken by a press gang
sailing further than any chart shows
keeping the crew fed through the next storm
finding a port that will still have {obj}
seeing {poss} name struck from every wanted notice
peeves: landlubbers who don't know port from starboard
a captain who won't share the plunder fairly
accessories: a coil of rope over the shoulder
a tricorn hat with a faded feather
a battered compass on a cord
a parrot perched on one shoulder
a dagger tucked in a boot
default_outfits: a loose linen shirt with rolled sleeves under a weathered leather waistcoat, wide canvas trousers, a wide sash at the waist and worn leather boots

_tables: The next four entries replace the shared tables in common.json for this setting only (same shape): sailors' hair (tarred queues, kerchiefs, no modern cuts or dye), heavy period beards, almost no eyewear, and a few sea-going marks (an eye patch, a hook hand).
